symptom: A new Go lint rule that reads the catalog reported NOTHING on a project that provably had the defect it detects, then reported correctly on the very next identical run. MPR017 found no decision expressions on a freshly built catalog and the real finding once the catalog was cached.
cause: Two separate causes, stacked, each silent. (1) linter.CatalogRequirer is an OPTIONAL interface: a rule that does not implement RequiredCatalogMode gets CatalogFast, so activities / widgets / xpath_expressions are never written and every expression-reading rule sees an empty project. Its own doc warns of exactly this ('silently returning empty results'). (2) Under it, ctx.AttributesFor fails with 'no such table: attributes' whenever lint BUILDS the catalog rather than loading it (ako/mxcli#2417), and once that query error is recorded the context stops answering later reads — a second `for e := range ctx.Entities()` loop did not execute its body once. Fixed (1) by declaring CatalogFull; worked around (2) by refusing with a linter.RuleFailure when entities read but attributes did not.
insight: A new rule's first measurement must be a POSITIVE control: build the defect and watch the rule fire. Two projects' worth of 'no false positives' looked like success and was a rule that could never fire at all — the same shape as #808. The discriminator that localised both causes in one step was running the new rule beside an established one in the same invocation: SEC001 reported its entities on the fresh catalog while the new rule reported nothing, which placed the fault in the new rule's inputs rather than in the catalog. Second: run every new rule twice on a brand-new project, because fresh-build and cached-catalog are different code paths and only the cached one works today. Third: anything a rule reads that the catalog writes only in full mode needs RequiredCatalogMode, and nothing fails loudly when it is missing — grep a new rule for activities/widgets/xpath_expressions/permissions before trusting a clean run. And a rule that cannot read its input must report linter.RuleFailure, never an empty result: `No issues found.` printed above an `Error:` line is what a CI gate reads as a pass.
